# Validation Contract: Deepen Effect Adoption (stacked on PR #1120)

Black-box behavioral assertions that define "done" for this mission. Validators test against these specifications, not against implementation structure. Do not assert "uses Effect.retry" or "uses ManagedRuntime"; assert observable retry, cancellation, error, lifecycle, and compatibility behavior.

**Repo:** `/home/ubuntu/hevy-mcp-effect-deepening`  
**Commands:** prefix every `mise exec` with `MISE_AUTO_INSTALL=false`.  
**Secrets:** never print, log, or persist `HEVY_API_KEY` values, `Authorization` / `api-key` headers, or bearer tokens. Deterministic assertions use fake credentials.

**Surfaces**

| Surface | Tool | When |
|---|---|---|
| Hevy client unit | vitest (`packages/hevy-client`) | Track 1 |
| Worker validation-cache | vitest (`packages/worker`, `pnpm run test:worker`) | Track 1 |
| Core / in-process MCP | vitest + mocked MCP (`test:mcp`, `test:contract`) | Track 2 |
| Node embedding / stdio / HTTP | vitest, spawned `node`, curl (`test:stdio`, `test:pack`) | Track 3 |
| CLI | vitest (`pnpm run test:cli`) | Track 3/4 |
| Live Hevy | `pnpm run test:live`, `pnpm run test:integration` | Milestone 4 only |

| Repo gates | `check`, `check:types`, `build`, `test:pr`, `test:performance`, `check:changeset`, `check:boundaries` | Every milestone + CROSS |

# Area: Client Runtime

## Surface

Who consumes this: `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` callers (`createHevyClient` Promise API used by Node, CLI, Worker, and tests); `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal` Effect request facade used by `@hevy-mcp/operations`; Worker bearer/OAuth validation via `validateHevyApiKeyResilient` in `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.ts`. End users never call this package directly; MCP tools and the CLI collapse through these Promise/Effect boundaries.

How it is tested: vitest in `packages/hevy-client` and `packages/worker`; TestClock and fake timers for delays; mocked `fetch` (no live Hevy in this area).

Focused suites:
- `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/request-effect.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/request-local-retry-state.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/retry-schedule.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/backoff.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/endpoint-policy.test.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.test.ts`

## Interactions enumerated

- Construct `createHevyClient({ apiKey, baseUrl?, fetch?, timeoutMs?, maxGetRetries?, sleep?, onLog?, onRequestStart?, onRequestComplete?, onRetryWait? })`.
- Call any of the 22 Promise methods with optional `{ signal, deadline, timeoutMs }`.
- Receive a successful JSON body, or a rejected `HevyHttpError` with `code` / `status` / execution metadata.
- Observe retries: transient GET/HEAD/OPTIONS reads and PUT/DELETE idempotent writes retry; POST/PATCH non-idempotent writes never retry.
- Observe retry budget: default `maxGetRetries = 3` (4 attempts); delays start at 300 ms, double each retry, cap at 5000 ms, plus bounded jitter.
- Observe 429 handling: client retries 429 and honors `Retry-After` as a lower bound, still jittered, clipped to remaining deadline.

# Area: Core Runtime

## Surface

`packages/core` is the MCP server the adapters embed. A client talks to it over the MCP protocol (in-process mocked client in `test:mcp` / `test:contract`, or any stdio/HTTP adapter).

**Intended catalog-cancellation policy:** a cache-miss load is interruptible. If the cancelling waiter is the **only** waiter, the shared Hevy load is cancelled. If the canceller is **one of several** waiters, that waiter is interrupted and the others keep the still-needed load. `refresh: true` still bypasses a hit and loads fresh data.

## Interactions enumerated

- MCP `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` (reads and writes, unknown names, invalid args, missing client/operation, Hevy failures, abort, deadline).
- MCP `resources/list` and `resources/read` of the four `hevy://` URIs, including abort of `hevy://exercise-templates`.
- MCP `prompts/list` and `prompts/get`.
- Catalog hit / miss / TTL / refresh / failed load / dual waiter topologies.
- Server close / `lifecycleSignal` abort interrupting in-flight cache loads.
- Observer, MCP logging, and cache-callback failures never change outcomes.
- Promise `createHevyMcpServer` façade still builds a working server.

## 1. What we are changing

PR #1120 already made `@hevy-mcp/operations` Effect-first and routed MCP tools and CLI commands through those programs, collapsing Effect at Promise adapter boundaries. This mission deepens Effect so it becomes the **actual control structure**, not a delay calculator or a Promise wrapper.

Three tracks, plus a last-mile live validation:

| Track | Package(s) | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| Client runtime | `packages/hevy-client`, `packages/worker` (validation-cache only) | Retry/timeout/interruption via `Effect.retry` + `Schedule` + `Effect.timeout*` + fiber interruption |
| Core runtime | `packages/core` | Scoped server construction, interruptible tool runs, typed error channel, Logger/Metrics |
| Node adapter | `packages/node` | Lifecycle, shutdown, telemetry, Streamable HTTP as scoped Effect programs |
| Live e2e | docs + live lanes | Verify against real Hevy API; update README/architecture docs |

**Out of scope**

- Worker adapter beyond the validation-cache retry loop (OAuth, bindings, request handling stay Promise-based).

## 2. System shape after this mission

```
process Scope  (packages/node)
  telemetry Layer (OTel/Sentry init + flush)
  signal handlers (SIGINT/SIGTERM)
  HTTP server / stdio transport
    └── server Scope  (packages/core)
          exercise-template Cache
          ManagedRuntime / long-lived Layer context
          MCP server instance
            └── request Scope  (per tool/resource invocation)
                  ToolExecutionContext (signal + deadline)
                  HevyOperationsService / HevyClientService
                  fiber interruption wired to mcpReq.signal
                    └── hevy-client request Effect
                          Effect.retry(schedule) + Effect.timeout*
                          AbortSignal bridged at fetch edge only
```

Every acquired resource lives in exactly one of these three scopes and has a finalizer there. Nothing is “leaked by design.”

## 3. Scope hierarchy (the central design)

### 3.1 Process scope — `packages/node`

Owned by `runNodeLifecycle`. Acquires:

- Process exception tracking (install/remove listeners).
- Telemetry providers (OTel tracer/meter, Sentry). Finalizer = `forceFlush` + shutdown.
- Graceful-shutdown listeners (SIGINT/SIGTERM). Forced-exit is `Effect.race(shutdown, Effect.sleep(5s))`, not a hand-rolled `setTimeout`.
- The MCP transport: stdio pipe, or the Streamable HTTP server (itself a Scope that owns sessions).

Public Promise façades (`createNodeMcpServer`, `runStdioServer`, `runServer`) remain. They collapse a process-scoped Effect via `Effect.runPromise`. Effect-typed variants may be added (e.g. `createNodeMcpServerEffect`) because public Effect exports are allowed.

`packages/node/src/index.ts` **must stay side-effect-free** (embedding contract). Telemetry init moves off module-import time into the Layer that the runtime program provides. The documented import-order constraint in `runtime.ts` goes away once telemetry is a Layer.

### 3.2 Server scope — `packages/core`

Owned by `createHevyMcpServer` (which becomes Effect-returning internally; the Promise wrapper stays for existing callers). Acquires:

- Exercise-template `Cache.make`. Lookup **must** read `ToolExecutionContextService` (or equivalent) so a cache-miss load is interruptible and deadline-bounded. The cache is finalized when the server Scope closes.
- A long-lived Layer context (HevyOperations, HevyClient, catalog, observer). Built with `ManagedRuntime` or an explicitly closed `Scope` — **never** `Effect.runSync(Scope.make())` that is never closed.
- The MCP `McpServer` instance.

`lifecycleSignal` from the Node adapter interrupts this scope on process shutdown.

### 3.3 Request scope — per tool / resource invocation

Created by `runtime.forExecution({ signal: context.mcpReq.signal, ... })`. Acquires:

- Merged abort signal (lifecycle ∪ request).
- Derived deadline (`nextExecution.deadline ?? serverDeadline ?? now + timeoutMs`).
- Request-local service overlay if needed.

`runToolEffect` **must** pass the request signal into `Effect.runPromise(program, { signal })` (or `runFork` + interrupt) so MCP cancellation interrupts the fiber, not only the underlying fetch.

The `exercise-templates` resource currently calls `.effect()` with no execution options. It must pass `scoped.execution` like the other resources.

## 4. Track 1 — Client runtime

### 4.1 Retry interpreter (`packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client-kubb.ts`)

**Today:** `Effect.gen` + `while (true)` + `Schedule.toStep` used as a delay iterator. `canRetryAttempt` is a separate predicate. `withTimeout` is a hand-rolled Promise.race. `createExecutionSignal` is a hand-rolled AbortController + `setTimeout`. `withExecutionSignal` (`execution.ts`) is exported and unused.

**Target:**

- One attempt is an Effect. The retry driver is `Effect.retry(schedule)` (or equivalent Effect 4 combinator). The Schedule owns:
  - Recurrence count (`Schedule.recurs(maxGetRetries)`).
  - Delay (`Schedule.addDelay` with existing `getRetryDelayMs`, including Retry-After union + jitter).
  - “Should I retry this error?” via `Schedule.whileInput` (or Effect 4 equivalent) wrapping `canRetryAttempt`.
- The “one free read retry after deadline” branch (`hevy-client-kubb.ts:877-903`) folds into schedule composition (`Schedule.recurs(1)` gated on deadline-exceeded + `safety === "read"` + no caller-supplied deadline), not a hardcoded side channel.
- Per-attempt timeout is `Effect.timeout*` around the fetch/body-parse, not `withTimeout`.
- Fiber interruption is the cancellation mechanism. AbortSignal is bridged **at the fetch edge only** (so native `fetch` still cancels). `abortOnInterruption` listeners and `createExecutionSignal` deadline timers go away or become thin adapters.
- Use `withExecutionSignal` inside `createRequestEffect`, or delete it. Do not leave two cleanup paths.

**Safety:** `operation.descriptor.safety` (from `@hevy-mcp/operations`) drives retry decisions for composed operations. HTTP-method mapping (`operationSafetyForMethod`) remains the fallback for raw client calls that have no descriptor. Non-idempotent writes are never retried.

**Behavior improvements are allowed** (user-approved). Flag every policy change in the worker handoff: retry counts, backoff curve, Retry-After handling, which errors retry, the free deadline-retry. Default to preserving current observable policy unless the improvement is a clear correctness/safety win (e.g. interruptible cache loads, no retry on non-idempotent writes at the operation layer).

**Promise boundary:** `HevyClient` stays Promise-typed for existing callers. Effect-typed request APIs may be exported. Tagged error classes at the Promise boundary stay discriminable (`ApiError`, `NetworkError`, `NotFoundError`, `RateLimitError`, `ValidationError`, plus the existing `HEVY_*` codes). Do not mutate errors in place (`applyRetryExhaustion` today mutates `error.code`); produce a new tagged error.

### 4.2 Worker validation-cache (`packages/worker/src/validation-cache.ts`)

**Today:** imperative `for` loop, delays `[300, 600]`, `delay()` that *resolves* on abort (forcing a post-sleep re-check). Excludes 429 while the client treats 429 as transient.

**Target:** `Effect.retry` with a composed Schedule (exponential 300ms, jittered, `whileInput(isRetryableValidationFailure)`, intersected with remaining deadline). Drop the custom `delay()`. Keep the 429 exclusion if it is still the right policy for a validation probe — document why in a comment next to the Schedule predicate.

Do **not** otherwise change Worker request handling, OAuth, or bindings.

## 5. Track 2 — Core runtime

### 5.1 Server construction (`packages/core/src/server.ts`)

`createHevyMcpServer` today is synchronous and does `Effect.runSync(Cache.make({ lookup: (_key) => templateListAll.effect() }))` with no execution options and no Scope.

**Target:**

- Construction is an Effect that requires `Scope`. The Promise wrapper (`createHevyMcpServer`) runs that Effect in a scope the adapter owns, or returns `{ server, close }` / uses `ManagedRuntime`.
- Cache lookup reads per-request execution context from the environment. A cancelled MCP request must not leave a full paginated template fetch running against Hevy.
- Missing `templates.listAll` is a tagged construction error, not `throw new Error(...)`.

### 5.2 Tool runtime (`packages/core/src/tools/tool-runtime.ts`)

**Today:** `buildServiceContext` does `Effect.runSync(Scope.make())` + `Layer.build` and never closes the scope (comment: “outlives this call”). `runToolEffect` calls `Effect.runPromise` with no signal. Handler type is `Effect.Effect<McpToolResponse, unknown, never>`. `createObservedHandler` is an ad-hoc Promise wrapper with a catch-retry of the handler.

**Target:**

- Long-lived services live in the server Scope (`ManagedRuntime` or equivalent). Request-local overlays (execution context, observer) are provided per invocation without leaking a Scope.
- `runToolEffect` is interruptible via the request signal.
- Error channel is a tagged union, not `unknown`. `withErrorHandling` becomes `Effect.catchTags` / `Cause` matching at the collapse boundary, then `createErrorResponse`.
- Observer `start`/`run`/`finish` become Effect taps (or a `Metric`/`Logger` layer). Telemetry failures must not affect tool outcome — use Effect sandboxing, not `catch {}`.
- Deadline arithmetic uses Effect `Clock` so `TestClock` can drive tests. `checkExecution` throws go away once the client/cache honor deadline via interruption.

`define-tool.ts`: Zod `.parse` moves into the Effect as a typed `ValidationError` (via `Effect.try` or Schema). `requireOperation` / `requireClient` become `Effect.fail` with tagged errors.

### 5.3 Error policy (`packages/core/src/utils/error-policy.ts`)

**Today:** `instanceof` cascades plus string-sniffing (`classificationText.includes("network")`). Defensive `try/catch` returning `undefined`.

**Target:** classify via tagged-error matching (`catchTags` / `Match` on `_tag`). Keep `SafeErrorDiagnostic` bounded-metadata machinery (categories, stack-frame whitelist) — that policy is load-bearing for not leaking secrets. The classification *input* changes (Cause/tag instead of `unknown`); the *output* (`SafeErrorDiagnostic`, user-facing message, MCP error code) stays compatible unless an improvement is flagged.

`console.error(JSON.stringify(createMcpToolFailureEvent(...)))` and the other core `console.error` sites (`mcp-client-logger.ts`, `prompts/workouts.ts`, `formatters.ts`, `templates.ts` onRefreshed) go through `Effect.log*` + a Logger layer that fans out to MCP `sendLoggingMessage` and stderr.

### 5.4 Catalog (`packages/core/src/utils/exercise-template-catalog.ts`)

Shared cache load must be interruptible. `replaceSharedCacheLoad` / `bypassCache` / `requestGeneration` exist because the lookup currently ignores execution; after lookup reads context, simplify if those workarounds become redundant — but keep bypass-cache behavior for callers that need a fresh fetch.

Prune vestigial types in `utils/cache.ts` (`AsyncCacheOptions`, unused `CacheGetOptions`) if nothing consumes them after the refactor.

- `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/request-effect.test.ts`

## Interactions enumerated

- Construct `createHevyClient({ apiKey, baseUrl?, fetch?, timeoutMs?, maxGetRetries?, sleep?, onLog?, onRequestStart?, onRequestComplete?, onRetryWait? })`.
- Call any of the 22 Promise methods with optional `{ signal, deadline, timeoutMs }`.
- Receive a successful JSON body, or a rejected `HevyHttpError` with `code` / `status` / execution metadata.
- Observe retries: transient GET/HEAD/OPTIONS reads and PUT/DELETE idempotent writes retry; POST/PATCH non-idempotent writes never retry.
- Observe retry budget: default `maxGetRetries = 3` (4 attempts); delays start at 300 ms, double each retry, cap at 5000 ms, plus bounded jitter.
- Observe 429 handling: client retries 429 and honors `Retry-After` as a lower bound, still jittered, clipped to remaining deadline.
- Observe per-attempt timeout and overall operation deadline.
- Observe the one extra read attempt after a client-derived attempt deadline. Caller-supplied `deadline` is never extended.
- Abort via `AbortSignal`: already-aborted, mid-fetch, while reading the body, during backoff. Concurrent requests stay isolated.
- Consume the internal Effect facade: same retry/timeout/abort counts; tagged errors.
- Operations pass `descriptor.safety` into composed Hevy calls; raw client calls fall back to HTTP-method mapping.
- Worker `validateHevyApiKeyResilient`: cache hit skips Hevy; miss validates; retries transient failures with delays `[300, 600]`; never retries 429; abort/deadline stop the loop; cache never stores the raw API key.

## Assertions

### VAL-CLIENT-001: Happy-path GET returns parsed JSON and sends api-key
A `getWorkouts` / `getUserInfo` / equivalent GET against a 200 JSON response resolves to the parsed body. The outbound request uses the configured `baseUrl` (default `https://api.hevyapp.com`), path under `/v1/`, query params, and an `api-key` header equal to the constructor `apiKey`. Exactly one `fetch` call occurs when the first response is 2xx.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test names `uses object-form options and safely encodes requests`, `forwards every curated operation through its generated API wrapper`; terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts`; no `HEVY_API_KEY` in logs.

### VAL-CLIENT-002: All 22 public Promise methods remain callable
Each method on `HevyClient` returns a `Promise` and, given a 200, resolves without throwing. `createRoutine` may resolve `undefined` when the body is empty. The public object has no enumerable `requestEffect`. Existing Promise signatures (`signal`, `deadline`, `timeoutMs`) keep working.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test names `forwards every curated operation through its generated API wrapper`, `keeps the public HevyClient Promise-only at type and runtime`; 22 `fetch` calls in the wrapper test.

### VAL-CLIENT-003: Default timeout is 60 seconds
With no constructor `timeoutMs` and no per-call `timeoutMs`/`deadline`, a hanging fetch is not aborted before 60_000 ms of attempt budget. The observable default attempt timeout remains one minute.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `allows slow collection endpoints a one-minute default deadline`.

### VAL-CLIENT-004: Per-call timeoutMs overrides the client default
A client constructed with a short `timeoutMs` still succeeds when the method is called with a larger `{ timeoutMs }` that covers the mocked latency.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `allows a per-operation timeout override`.

### VAL-CLIENT-005: Hanging fetch times out as HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
When `fetch` never settles and no caller `deadline` is set, the Promise rejects with `HevyHttpError` `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", outcome: "deadline_exceeded", phase: "dispatch" }`.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `times out when fetch never settles`.

### VAL-CLIENT-006: Hanging response body times out as HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
When headers return 200 but the body stream never completes, the Promise rejects with `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", outcome: "deadline_exceeded", phase: "response-content" }`.
Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `times out while consuming a response body`.

### VAL-CLIENT-007: One free read retry after a client-derived attempt deadline
On a read (GET) with `maxGetRetries > 0` and no caller `deadline`, the first attempt-timeout is followed by exactly one more fetch with a fresh attempt budget. That extra attempt does not emit `onLog` message `"Retrying Hevy API request"` and does not open `onRetryWait`. If the second attempt returns 200, the method resolves. Observation sequence includes `deadline_exceeded` then `success`. This remains true if the implementation folds the extra attempt into schedule composition: consumers still see one extra read fetch, no backoff sleep, no retry log.
Tool: vitest

# Area: Core Runtime

## Surface

`packages/core` is the MCP server the adapters embed. A client talks to it over the MCP protocol (in-process mocked client in `test:mcp` / `test:contract`, or any stdio/HTTP adapter).

**Intended catalog-cancellation policy:** a cache-miss load is interruptible. If the cancelling waiter is the **only** waiter, the shared Hevy load is cancelled. If the canceller is **one of several** waiters, that waiter is interrupted and the others keep the still-needed load. `refresh: true` still bypasses a hit and loads fresh data.

## Interactions enumerated

- MCP `initialize`, `tools/list`, `tools/call` (reads and writes, unknown names, invalid args, missing client/operation, Hevy failures, abort, deadline).
- MCP `resources/list` and `resources/read` of the four `hevy://` URIs, including abort of `hevy://exercise-templates`.
- MCP `prompts/list` and `prompts/get`.
- Catalog hit / miss / TTL / refresh / failed load / dual waiter topologies.
- Server close / `lifecycleSignal` abort interrupting in-flight cache loads.
- Observer, MCP logging, and cache-callback failures never change outcomes.
- Promise `createHevyMcpServer` façade still builds a working server.

- 404: resource not found; routine PUT 404 keeps the "deleted or the routine ID is incorrect" guidance.

- 5xx: Hevy API error, retry later.
- Retry exhausted: "after N attempts" / "after multiple attempts".

- Ordinary `Error` / non-Error throws: `The request failed unexpectedly. Please try again.`

# Review: Client Runtime + Worker Validation-Cache (VAL-CLIENT-* / VAL-WORKER-*)

Review of `validation-contract.md` Area: Client Runtime against `architecture.md` Track 1, `mission.md` Milestone 1, and the current interpreters in `/home/ubuntu/hevy-mcp-effect-deepening/packages/hevy-client` and `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.ts`.

Focus: consumer-flow topology, missing interactions/states, implementation-shaped wording, duplicate IDs, ambiguous pass/fail. New VAL-* text only for real gaps.

---

## Verdict

The section is **almost complete** for Track 1. Happy-path GET, the 22 Promise methods, timeout/deadline/abort, read vs write retry, 429 Retry-After, Effect tagged-error parity, secret redaction, endpoint identities, and the worker cache hit/miss/429/abort-during-delay/waitUntil paths are all named with observable pass/fail.

Three real behavioral holes remain (new IDs below):

1. **Idempotent-write hanging fetch** is not covered. VAL-CLIENT-010 is titled as all writes but the body is POST-only; the free deadline retry is gated on `safety === "read"` in current code and in architecture §4.1. A PUT timeout could silently gain a second fetch when the extra attempt is folded into Schedule composition.
2. **`maxGetRetries: 0` must disable both HTTP retries and the free deadline retry.** 013 covers fractional floor → one fetch on 503; 007 only specifies the `> 0` case. Folding the extra read into `Schedule.recurs(1)` can accidentally fire when the budget is zero.
3. **Worker: valid-after-retry must be cached.** 002 caches a first-try `"valid"`; 004 retries 503 then returns `"valid"`; neither says the subsequent call is a hit. That is a distinct cache state (miss → transient → valid → hit).

Worker delay **exactness** (`[300, 600]`) and the **injected `sleep` hook** are not missing flows; they are ambiguous/compatibility nits (see Residual nits). Do not mint IDs for those unless the orchestrator wants to freeze current delays against architecture §4.2’s jittered Schedule.

No duplicate VAL-CLIENT / VAL-WORKER IDs. Overlaps with VAL-CROSS-014 (worker 429 vs client 429, `maxGetRetries: 0` on the probe client) are composed views, not duplicates.

---

## Topology coverage

| Consumer flow | Covered? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| `createHevyClient` + GET 200 + `api-key` + default baseUrl | Yes | VAL-CLIENT-001 |
| All 22 Promise methods; no enumerable `requestEffect` | Yes | VAL-CLIENT-002 |
| Per-attempt 60s default; per-call `timeoutMs` override | Yes | 003, 004 |
| Hang on fetch / body → `HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` | Yes | 005, 006 |
| Free read retry after client-derived attempt deadline; not repeated; caller deadline never extended | Yes | 007, 008, 009 |
| POST/PATCH never retry HTTP/network; PUT retries with unknown commit | Yes | 011, 012 |
| Read retry budget, retryable statuses, 429 Retry-After, backoff vs deadline | Yes | 013–017 |
| Abort before / mid-fetch / during backoff; concurrent isolation | Yes | 018–021 |
| Exhaustion is a new tagged error; Effect `catchTag` parity | Yes | 022, 023 |
| Expected GET 404; canonical endpoints; secrets; execution aliases | Yes | 024–027 |
| `descriptor.safety` for composed operations; HTTP-method fallback | Yes | 028 |
| Invalid non-`/v1/` URL; do not cancel a locked 200 body | Yes | 029, 030 |
| Worker cache hit / miss / invalid / hash+TTL+cap / KV faults | Yes | VAL-WORKER-001–003 |
| Worker transient retry; 429 excluded; abort-during-wait; deadline; `waitUntil` | Yes | 004–008 |
| **PUT/DELETE hanging fetch — no free deadline retry** | **No** | see VAL-CLIENT-031 |
| **`maxGetRetries: 0` — no HTTP retry and no free deadline retry** | **No** | see VAL-CLIENT-032 |
| **Worker 503-then-valid is cached for the next call** | **No** | see VAL-WORKER-009 |
| HEAD/OPTIONS as reads | N/A (no public methods); HTTP-method fallback is in 028 | |

Abort mid-body is in the interactions list and in VAL-CLIENT-019 evidence (`cancels response-content consumption through the caller signal`). Fine.

---

## Proposed new assertions

### VAL-CLIENT-031: Idempotent writes never get the free deadline retry

**Why this is a gap.** Architecture §4.1: the extra attempt is gated on deadline-exceeded **and** `safety === "read"` **and** no caller deadline. VAL-CLIENT-010’s title says “Writes” but the body only names `createWorkout` (POST). VAL-CLIENT-012 retries PUT on HTTP 503, which a validator could misread as “PUT also gets the deadline extra attempt.” After Schedule composition, that is the easy silent policy change.

**Black-box assertion.** `updateWorkout` / `updateRoutine` / `updateBodyMeasurement` (PUT) against a hanging `fetch`, with `maxGetRetries > 0` and no caller `deadline`, rejects `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED" }` after **exactly one** `fetch`. No `onLog` `"Retrying Hevy API request"`, no `onRetryWait`, no second attempt. Same if a raw client call is made with HTTP DELETE (idempotent-write fallback). POST remains covered by VAL-CLIENT-010.

**Tool / evidence.** vitest; extend `does not retry writes after a deadline` (or a sibling named for PUT). Fail: two fetches on a hanging PUT.

Do **not** fold this into 012 (012 is HTTP 503 retry-then-success). Keep 010 as non-idempotent; this ID is the read-only extra-attempt gate on idempotent writes.

### VAL-CLIENT-032: Zero retry budget means a single attempt, including on timeout

**Why this is a gap.** VAL-CLIENT-013: fractional `maxGetRetries` floors to 0 → one fetch on repeating 503. VAL-CLIENT-007: free deadline retry requires `maxGetRetries > 0`. Nothing says a hanging GET with `maxGetRetries: 0` must not take the extra attempt. Architecture explicitly folds that branch into `Schedule.recurs(1)` gated on budget; a `recurs(1)` that ignores the zero budget would still look green on 007/013.

**Black-box assertion.** With `maxGetRetries: 0` and no caller `deadline`: (a) GET against hanging `fetch` rejects `HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` after exactly one fetch (no free deadline retry); (b) GET against repeating HTTP 503 rejects after exactly one fetch (no scheduled retry). `onRetryWait` is not opened. Constructor `maxGetRetries: 0` and per-client option 0 are equivalent.

**Tool / evidence.** vitest; pair with 007/013 rather than changing 007’s `> 0` success path.

### VAL-WORKER-009: Valid-after-retry is cached; the next call is a hit

**Why this is a gap.** VAL-WORKER-002: first-try `"valid"` is cached; `"invalid"` and throws are not. VAL-WORKER-004: 503 then `"valid"` calls `validate` twice and returns `"valid"`. The cache **state after a retried success** is unstated. A Schedule rewrite that returns `"valid"` without calling `cacheValidation` would still pass 004.

**Black-box assertion.** `validateHevyApiKeyResilient` on a cache miss: first `validate` throws a retryable `HevyHttpError` (503 / 408 / 5xx / status-less), second returns `"valid"`. The function returns `"valid"`. A following `validateHevyApiKeyResilient` for **that same key** returns `"valid"` **without** calling `validate` (cache hit). A different key still misses. The retried success is not stored as the raw API key (VAL-WORKER-003 still holds). An eventual `"invalid"` after a retried 503 is **not** cached (still 002).

**Tool / evidence.** vitest on `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.test.ts`; compose the existing 503-then-success stub with `hasCachedValidation` / a second resilient call.

---

## Implementation-shaped / ambiguous (do not add IDs; tighten in place)

These are **not** missing flows. Fix wording in the existing IDs if the contract is edited.

1. **VAL-CLIENT-010 body vs title.** Title is “Writes never get a deadline retry”; body is POST-only. Either add PUT to 010 **or** keep 010 as non-idempotent and add VAL-CLIENT-031 (preferred, so 012’s PUT HTTP retry stays distinct). Leaving 010 as-is is ambiguous pass/fail.
2. **VAL-CLIENT-003** asserts the named constant `DEFAULT_API_TIMEOUT_MS` and only a lower bound (“not aborted before 60_000 ms”). Observable default attempt budget is enough; drop the constant name. Combined with 005/007 it is still passable.
3. **VAL-CLIENT-023** “or an interrupt Cause that the Promise adapter projects” is Cause-shaped. Keep the observable: hanging Effect + fiber interrupt → `HEVY_REQUEST_ABORTED` / `outcome: "cancelled"` at the Promise boundary.
4. **VAL-CLIENT-028 evidence** (“if the interpreter starts reading `descriptor.safety`”) is implementation. The assertion body is behavioral; leave the body, drop the interpreter note.
5. **VAL-WORKER-004** cites `VALIDATION_RETRY_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3` and exact delays `[300, 600]`. Architecture §4.2 wants a jittered exponential Schedule. Exact milliseconds will **fail the intended rewrite** if jitter is added. Keep “maximum 3 attempts; first delay on the order of 300 ms, second on the order of 600 ms” (or allow the same jitter bounds as VAL-CLIENT-015). Still require: 3 consecutive 503s → 3 `validate` calls, no 4th (today only implied).
6. **VAL-WORKER-004 / 005** “uses `createSafeErrorDiagnostic`” / “comment next to the retry predicate” are implementation evidence. Behavioral bar: retry/429 logs never contain the raw key; 429 is excluded even though the Hevy client retries 429.
7. **VAL-WORKER-006** is correctly behavioral (wait must fail on abort, not resolve-then-recheck). Keep. Do not mention `delay()`.

---

## Residual nits (no new IDs)

- **Constructor `sleep`.** Public `HevyClientOptions.sleep` is listed in Interactions and used by characterization tests. Architecture replaces waits with Effect Clock / TestClock. Either keep sleep as an optional override (abort still fails the wait) or flag its removal as a behavior change. Not a user-facing MCP/CLI flow; do not mint VAL-CLIENT-033 unless embedder compatibility is in scope.

- **422 / other 4xx except 408 and 429 are not retried.** 014 lists 400/401/403/404/409. `isTransientRetryStatus` already excludes 422. Extend the 014 list in place.
- **Worker exhaustion of 3 transients** belongs in a tightened 004, not a new ID.
- **Worker abort during the in-flight `validate()`** (not during backoff) is implied by “abort/deadline stop the loop” plus client 018/019. 006 owns the known resolve-on-abort hazard; do not split.
- **OAUTH_KV absent / non-KV-shaped → memory fallback** is tested and sketched in 003 (“Memory fallback uses the same hashed key”). Enough.

- **HEAD/OPTIONS/PATCH/DELETE** have no curated Promise methods. 011/012/028 HTTP-method fallback is enough.
- **Custom `fetch` on every attempt** is implied by 001+013.
- **Malformed JSON 200**, `timeoutMs <= 0` normalization, Retry-After HTTP-date in the past, and timer-leak after settlement are out of the mission’s retry/timeout/interrupt brief.
- **VAL-CLIENT-011 vs 028** both say non-idempotent writes never retry; 028 adds `descriptor.safety`. Fine overlap, not duplicate IDs.
- **VAL-WORKER-005 vs VAL-CLIENT-015** 429 divergence is intentional; VAL-CROSS-014 owns the composed pair.

## Surface
Who consumes this: `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client` callers (`createHevyClient` Promise API used by Node, CLI, Worker, and tests); `@hevy-mcp/hevy-client/internal` Effect request facade used by `@hevy-mcp/operations`; Worker bearer/OAuth validation via `validateHevyApiKeyResilient` in `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.ts`. How it is tested: vitest in `packages/hevy-client` and `packages/worker`; TestClock and fake timers for delays; mocked `fetch` (no live Hevy in this area). Tool: vitest (`pnpm run test:unit` scoped to the files below) and, for live later, `pnpm run test:live`.

Focused suites:
- `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/internal-request-effect.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/request-effect.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/request-local-retry-state.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/retry-schedule.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/backoff.test.ts`
- `packages/hevy-client/src/endpoint-policy.test.ts`
- `packages/worker/src/validation-cache.test.ts`

## Interactions enumerated
- Construct `createHevyClient({ apiKey, baseUrl?, fetch?, timeoutMs?, maxGetRetries?, sleep?, onLog?, onRequestStart?, onRequestComplete?, onRetryWait? })`.
- Call any of the 22 Promise methods (`getWorkouts`, `getWorkout`, `createWorkout`, `updateWorkout`, `getWorkoutCount`, `getWorkoutEvents`, `getRoutines`, `getRoutineById`, `createRoutine`, `updateRoutine`, `getExerciseTemplates`, `getExerciseTemplate`, `getExerciseHistory`, `createExerciseTemplate`, `getRoutineFolders`, `createRoutineFolder`, `getRoutineFolder`, `getBodyMeasurements`, `getBodyMeasurement`, `createBodyMeasurement`, `updateBodyMeasurement`, `getUserInfo`) with optional `{ signal, deadline, timeoutMs }`.
- Receive a successful JSON body, or a rejected `HevyHttpError` with `code` / `status` / execution metadata.
- Observe retries: transient GET/HEAD/OPTIONS reads and PUT/DELETE idempotent writes retry; POST/PATCH non-idempotent writes never retry.
- Observe retry budget: default `maxGetRetries = 3` (4 attempts); delays start at 300 ms, double each retry, cap at 5000 ms, plus bounded jitter (< 250 ms; smaller when Retry-After is present).
- Observe 429 handling: client retries 429 and honors `Retry-After` (seconds or HTTP-date) as a lower bound, still jittered, clipped to remaining deadline.
- Observe per-attempt timeout (`timeoutMs`, default 60_000 ms) on both fetch settle and body consumption; overall operation deadline is `now + timeoutMs * (maxGetRetries + 1)` unless the caller supplies `deadline`.
- Observe the one extra read attempt after a client-derived attempt deadline (no backoff log, no retry-wait). Caller-supplied `deadline` is authoritative and is never extended.
- Abort via `AbortSignal`: already-aborted before dispatch, abort mid-fetch, abort while reading the body, abort during backoff. Concurrent requests stay isolated.
- Consume the internal Effect facade (`getRequestEffectClient`): same retry/timeout/abort counts as Promise methods; failures are tagged `ApiError` | `NetworkError` | `NotFoundError` | `RateLimitError` | `ValidationError`.
- Operations pass `descriptor.safety` (`read` | `idempotent-write` | `non-idempotent-write`) into composed Hevy calls; raw client calls fall back to HTTP-method mapping.
- Worker `validateHevyApiKeyResilient`: cache hit skips Hevy; miss validates; retries transient failures with delays `[300, 600]` (3 attempts); never retries 429; never caches invalid/thrown verdicts; abort/deadline stop the loop; KV/memory cache never stores the raw API key.

## Assertions

### VAL-CLIENT-001: Happy-path GET returns parsed JSON and sends api-key
A `getWorkouts` / `getUserInfo` / equivalent GET against a 200 JSON response resolves to the parsed body. The outbound request uses the configured `baseUrl` (default `https://api.hevyapp.com`), path under `/v1/`, query params, and an `api-key` header equal to the constructor `apiKey`. Exactly one `fetch` call occurs when the first response is 2xx.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: test names `uses object-form options and safely encodes requests`, `forwards every curated operation through its generated API wrapper`; terminal output of `packages/hevy-client/src/hevy-client.test.ts`; no `HEVY_API_KEY` in logs.

### VAL-CLIENT-002: All 22 public Promise methods remain callable
Each method on `HevyClient` returns a `Promise` and, given a 200, resolves without throwing. `createRoutine` may resolve `undefined` when the body is empty. The public object has no enumerable `requestEffect`. Existing Promise signatures (`signal`, `deadline`, `timeoutMs`) keep working.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: test names `forwards every curated operation through its generated API wrapper`, `keeps the public HevyClient Promise-only at type and runtime`; 22 `fetch` calls in the wrapper test.

### VAL-CLIENT-003: Default timeout is 60 seconds
With no constructor `timeoutMs` and no per-call `timeoutMs`/`deadline`, a hanging fetch is not aborted before 60_000 ms of attempt budget. `DEFAULT_API_TIMEOUT_MS` remains 60_000.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `allows slow collection endpoints a one-minute default deadline`; any hanging-fetch timeout test that uses an explicit smaller `timeoutMs` must not be treated as changing the default.

### VAL-CLIENT-004: Per-call timeoutMs overrides the client default
A client constructed with a short `timeoutMs` still succeeds when the method is called with a larger `{ timeoutMs }` that covers the mocked latency.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `allows a per-operation timeout override`.

### VAL-CLIENT-005: Hanging fetch times out as HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
When `fetch` never settles and no caller `deadline` is set, the Promise rejects with `HevyHttpError` `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", outcome: "deadline_exceeded", phase: "dispatch" }`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `times out when fetch never settles`.

### VAL-CLIENT-006: Hanging response body times out as HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED
When headers return 200 but the body stream never completes, the Promise rejects with `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", outcome: "deadline_exceeded", phase: "response-content" }`.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `times out while consuming a response body`.

### VAL-CLIENT-007: One free read retry after a client-derived attempt deadline
On a read (GET) with `maxGetRetries > 0` and no caller `deadline`, the first attempt-timeout is followed by exactly one more fetch with a fresh attempt budget. That extra attempt does not emit `onLog` message `"Retrying Hevy API request"` and does not open `onRetryWait`. If the second attempt returns 200, the method resolves. Observation sequence includes `deadline_exceeded` then `success`.

This remains true if the implementation folds the extra attempt into schedule composition: consumers still see one extra read fetch, no backoff sleep, no retry log.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: test name `retries a read once with a fresh deadline budget after a deadline`.

### VAL-CLIENT-008: Free read retry is bounded and not repeated
If the extra read attempt also times out, the rejection is `{ code: "HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED", outcome: "deadline_exceeded" }` and `fetch` is called exactly twice. After that extra attempt, a subsequent HTTP 500 is reported as `status: 500` / `outcome: "terminal_failure"`, not as another deadline, and is not retried again.

Tool: vitest
Evidence: test names `returns the deadline error when the bounded read retry also times out`, `does not misclassify a non-deadline retry failure as deadline exceeded`, `uses one timeout budget for hanging response bodies`.

`getWorkout(..., { deadline })` against a hanging fetch fails with `HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` after a single fetch. No retry log, no sleep, no retry-wait. Pre-dispatch synchronous fetch throws are `{ phase: "before-dispatch", commit_state: "not_sent" }`. Reads that never confirmed a response are `commit_state: "not_sent"`; writes after dispatch without confirmation are `unknown`.

Examples: `user.get` / `workouts.list` / `routines.get` are `read` and may retry transients; `routines.create` / `folders.create` are `non-idempotent-write` and never retry. Focus: first-visit, cancellation across layers, shutdown stopping Hevy work, write no-retry, worker 429 divergence, boundaries, pack, changeset, PR baseline, secret leakage, Promise façades.

## Verdict

The CROSS section already names the right composed path (Promise adapter → core runtime → operations `.effect()` → hevy-client request Effect → native `fetch`) and the process → server → request → fetch-edge AbortSignal hierarchy. Most VAL-CROSS-* items are **legitimate composed views** of area assertions, not redundant unit tests.

Two real composed-flow gaps remain:

1. **Process shutdown must stop in-flight Hevy work** (stdio/HTTP SIGTERM/SIGINT → lifecycle → server Scope → request fiber → native `fetch`). VAL-CROSS-005 closes the transport and flushes telemetry; it never says the hanging Hevy call aborts. VAL-CORE-024 and VAL-NODE-012 each cover one layer only.
2. **Stdio is missing from the multi-transport first-visit/read contract.** VAL-CROSS-003 lists in-memory MCP, Node Streamable HTTP, and the Worker HTTP harness — not spawned stdio `tools/call`. VAL-NODE-011 is `initialize` + `tools/list` only.

One Promise-collapse gap is worth a CROSS id because no single area owns all three collapse surfaces:

3. **Cause / Effect internals must not leak through MCP, CLI, or Node stderr** after collapse. Core covers MCP (`VAL-CORE-002` / `010` / `012`); CLI and Node do not assert the same “no `Cause` / `Layer` / fiber dump” rule.

Everything else in the focus list is already asserted, either as a CROSS flow or as an area assertion whose composition is implied. Do not mint CROSS ids that only restated VAL-CLIENT / VAL-CORE / VAL-NODE / VAL-WORKER.

---

## Proposed new assertions

### VAL-CROSS-023: Process shutdown aborts in-flight Hevy work

**Why it is composed (not an area restatement).** Architecture §2–§3: process Scope owns SIGINT/SIGTERM and `lifecycleSignal`; that signal interrupts the server Scope; request fibers must stop; AbortSignal is bridged at the fetch edge only. VAL-CROSS-005 asserts transport close + telemetry flush + 5s forced-exit. VAL-NODE-012 asserts “active work tied to the lifecycle abort signal is cancelled” without mentioning Hevy `fetch`. VAL-CORE-024 asserts `lifecycleSignal` abort in core isolation. VAL-CROSS-006 covers **HTTP session** close, not process SIGTERM on stdio. VAL-CROSS-007 covers **catalog** paging after server close, not a hanging `get-workouts` fetch.

**Black-box assertion.** After stdio or HTTP `hevy-mcp` is running with a fake key, start a `tools/call` (or catalog miss) against a hanging mocked Hevy GET. Deliver SIGINT or SIGTERM. Pass: the mocked fetch is aborted (`AbortError` / caller signal aborted) and does not complete after the signal; the process still follows VAL-CROSS-005 (close, bounded telemetry flush, no orphaned listener/server). Fail: Hevy retries or body read continue after shutdown, or shutdown waits on Hevy retry/backoff.

**Tool / evidence.** vitest + spawned node (`pnpm run test:stdio`); nock/mocked client delayed GET; pair with VAL-CROSS-005 rather than folding Hevy-abort into 005 (different observable: fetch abort vs transport/telemetry).

Do **not** replace VAL-CROSS-006 or VAL-CROSS-007; those are session-scoped and cache-scoped.

### VAL-CROSS-024: Stdio first-visit can call get-workouts

**Why it is composed.** First-visit in the CROSS surface is “import / construct / list / call a read tool.” VAL-CROSS-001–002 are embedding + in-process mocked MCP. **Why it is composed.** Architecture §7 / §13: Promise collapse happens once at the adapter/tool/resource boundary; Cause is converted to existing error classes. # Deepen Effect Adoption in hevy-mcp

## Plan Overview

PR #1120 ("Effect-first Hevy operations layer") made domain operations Effect-first but left three areas Promise/imperative: the hevy-client request interpreter (hand-rolled `while(true)` retry loop that uses `Schedule` only as a delay calculator, hand-rolled `withTimeout`), core server internals (cache built via `Effect.runSync` outside any Scope, leaked per-request scopes, `unknown` error channels, string-sniffing error policy, no interruption wiring on `runPromise`), and the entire Node adapter (zero Effect imports — manual lifecycle, shutdown, telemetry, and an ~800-line hand-managed HTTP session graph).

This mission deepens Effect adoption in those three areas (plus the Worker's ad-hoc validation retry loop), making the code easier to reason about and operations safer: typed error channels, guaranteed cleanup via `Scope`/`acquireRelease`, cancellation/timeout discipline via fiber interruption and `Effect.timeout*`, retry via `Effect.retry(Schedule)`, and structured logging/metrics via Effect Logger/Metrics.

**Base:** branch `feat/effect-deepening` in worktree `/home/ubuntu/hevy-mcp-effect-deepening`, stacked on `origin/feat/effect-ops-layer` (PR #1120). Effect types may appear in public exports (user-approved deviation from the PR's Promise-only stance). Behavior improvements over the current retry/timeout policy are allowed when they are clear wins; they must be flagged in handoffs for review.

## Architecture

```
┌────────────────────────── adapters (Promise façades + Effect-typed variants)
│  packages/node    packages/worker    packages/cli
│  lifecycle/shutdown/telemetry/HTTP   validation retry   (unchanged this mission)
│  as scoped Effect programs           via Effect.retry
└──────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
               │ consume
┌──────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  packages/core — MCP server internals                    │
│  server construction as scoped Layer (ManagedRuntime/    │
│  Scope-owned cache, finalized on shutdown)               │
│  tool runtime: interruption-wired runs, per-request      │
│  scopes, typed error union + catchTags policy,           │
│  Effect Logger/Metrics bridging to MCP logging           │
└──────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────┘
               │ consume
┌──────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  packages/operations (already Effect-first from PR)      │
│  + packages/hevy-client — request interpreter            │
│  Effect.retry(schedule) owns retry decisions;            │
│  Effect.timeout* + fiber interruption replace            │
│  withTimeout/createExecutionSignal timers;               │
│  descriptor.safety drives retry policy                   │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

**Scope hierarchy (the central design idea):** process Scope (node lifecycle: telemetry, signal handlers) → server Scope (core: template cache, shared runtime) → request Scope (tool invocations, interruption-wired to `mcpReq.signal`). # Review 2: Client Runtime + Worker Validation-Cache

Second pass of `validation-contract.md` Area: Client Runtime **after** first-pass IDs VAL-CLIENT-031, VAL-CLIENT-032, VAL-WORKER-009 and the in-place tightens of 003 / 010 / 014 / 023 / 028 / 004 / 005.

Scope: remaining **missing consumer flows**. Full new VAL-* text only for those. Do not re-propose 031 / 032 / 009.

---

## Verdict

The first pass closed the three holes it named (PUT hanging fetch, `maxGetRetries: 0`, Worker valid-after-retry cache). Three real flows are still unasserted:

1. **Idempotent-write retry budget and exhaustion.** 012 is one 503 then 200. 013’s `maxGetRetries` / `HEVY_RETRY_EXHAUSTED` story is GET-only. 031 only forbids the *free deadline* extra attempt on PUT. A Schedule rewrite can retry PUT once, forever, or on a different budget and still pass 012 + 031.
2. **Which timeout actually fires.** 003 is the 60s default with *no* constructor `timeoutMs`. 004 is only “larger per-call still succeeds.” 005 does not say whether the budget came from constructor, per-call, or default. Constructor `timeoutMs` can be ignored and all three stay green.
3. **Worker exhausted transients are not an invalid-key verdict.** 004 now requires three `validate` calls and no fourth. 002 says `"invalid"` and throws are not cached. Nothing forbids mapping 3×503 onto `"invalid"` (Worker would treat a Hevy outage as a bad bearer).

No duplicate VAL-CLIENT / VAL-WORKER IDs. Do not mint IDs for Effect free-retry parity, Worker Retry-After, or `timeoutMs`+`deadline` — those are in-place tightens (Residual nits).

---

## Topology after first pass

| Consumer flow | Covered? | Where |
|---|---|---|
| GET 200, 22 Promise methods, default 60s, per-call override (larger) | Yes | 001–004 |
| Hang fetch / body → `HEVY_DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` | Yes | 005, 006 |
| Free read retry; bounded; caller deadline never extended | Yes | 007–009 |
| POST no deadline retry; POST no HTTP retry; PUT HTTP 503→200 | Yes | 010–012 |
| GET retry budget, retryable statuses (incl. 422), 429 Retry-After, backoff vs deadline, fresh attempt timeout | Yes | 013–017 |
| Abort before / mid / backoff; concurrent isolation | Yes | 018–021 |
| Exhaustion is a new object; Effect `catchTag` + listed fetch-count parity | Yes | 022, 023 |
| Expected 404, canonical endpoints, secrets, aliases, `descriptor.safety`, invalid URL, locked 200 body | Yes | 024–030 |
| PUT/DELETE hanging fetch — no free deadline retry | Yes (pass 1) | 031 |
| `maxGetRetries: 0` — no HTTP retry and no free deadline retry | Yes (pass 1) | 032 |
| Worker hit / miss / invalid / hash+TTL+cap / KV faults | Yes | 001–003 |
| Worker transient retry counts; 429 excluded; abort-during-wait; deadline; `waitUntil` | Yes | 004–008 |
| Worker 503-then-valid is a subsequent hit | Yes (pass 1) | 009 |
| **PUT repeating 503 / 429 — same budget as reads, then `HEVY_RETRY_EXHAUSTED`** | **No** | VAL-CLIENT-033 |
| **Constructor `timeoutMs` is the attempt budget when the call omits `timeoutMs`** | **No** | VAL-CLIENT-034 |
